title.narrative: Mass Communication Strategy Adapted for Sexual and Reproductive Health and Related Rights in Burundi- NYUNGANIRA

description.narrative:
Project Objectives:
General Objective: The overarching goal of this intervention is to contribute to the evolution of knowledge, attitudes, norms, and practices through adapted communication in order to eliminate violence related to sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) for women, girls, and adolescents in Burundi.
Specific Objectives:
Objective 1: Develop and Implement a Fact-Based Communication Strategy Establish a communication strategy grounded in factual information, free from judgment, stereotypes, and stigma. This strategy will empower girls, women, and boys with the knowledge and attitudes necessary to make informed decisions regarding SRHR, enabling them to enjoy their sexuality in a fulfilling and risk-free manner.
Objective 2: Empower Youth to Challenge Inequitable Social Norms Provide relevant information to young girls and boys, equipping them with the knowledge and attitudes to question inequitable social norms and practices. This will allow them to advocate for their rights and become pioneers of societal transformation, particularly in the area of SRHR.
Objective 3: Strengthen Media and Influencers as Allies for SRHR Build the capacity of various media and influencers to become strong allies in promoting SRHR. These allies will help disseminate information that challenges harmful gender norms and behaviors, preventing violence against women and girls, and advocating for the rights to sexual and reproductive health. The goal is to amplify SRHR messages and contribute to connecting information with service utilization, helping to ensure wider access to SRHR services.
Objective 4: Achieve Social Change for an Informed Society on SRHR The ultimate aim is to create a society where informed girls, women, and boys can fully enjoy their sexual and reproductive rights. They will be equipped to make well-informed decisions regarding their sexuality, contributing to long-lasting change in attitudes and behaviors surrounding SRHR as outlined in our theory of change.

The target groups of Nyunganira program are the following:
- Young people ( girls & boys) - Young adults ( girls & boys) Women - Parents - People living with disabilities - Influencers (e.g., humorists, public figures) - Media professionals (journalists and media workers) - Vulnerable populations (e.g., those affected by violence and sexual harassment) - Communities at large (rural areas, including school clubs and women's groups) - Health service providers (for outreach and education)

This activity involves the development and implementation of a Mass Communication Strategy tailored specifically for promoting Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) in Burundi. The strategy aims to engage and inform diverse target groups, including young people, women, and vulnerable communities, about SRHR issues through various media channels. By leveraging radio, Printed Magazine, social media, and community-based platforms, the initiative focuses on raising awareness, addressing misinformation, and fostering positive attitudes toward sexual and reproductive health.

sector.narrative: The "Nyunganira" project, aims to improve sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) knowledge, attitudes, and practices among Burundian youth, girls, and women, through strategic communication and media campaigns addressing societal norms, with a focus on reducing violence and empowering marginalized groups. It operates within the health and gender sectors.

title.narrative: Description of reduced barriers to accessing SRHR (incl. HIV/AIDS) information, services and supplies in humanitarian settings

comment.narrative:
In recent years, young people have had various questions about Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH), but many reported not knowing where to find clear and complete information. Due to a lack of trust in service providers for different reasons, they often turned to the internet, exposing themselves to the risks of misinformation on social media.
With Nyunganira, through digital spaces such as online information platforms, WhatsApp groups, focus group discussions, and community awareness-raising sessions—and most importantly, the Listening and Orientation Mechanism (LOM)—barriers to SRHR services and information were significantly reduced.
In 2024, the newly established LOM received 860 requests, and 84% of users confirmed their satisfaction with the support they received.
